A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CORAL framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original acceptance-length, speedup, latency, and ablation results, including the main comparisons in Table 2 and appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical evaluation and adds feature-discrepancy measurements, additional benchmark results, and a router failure-case analysis.

M1.justification: The CSRA objective, combined loss, LM-head grouping and routing procedure, and two-stage training remain unchanged. Figure 3 corrects feature labels without changing the procedure described in the text.

E1.justification: Appendix G and Table 8 add evaluation on Alpaca, Natural Questions, and CNN/DM, extending coverage to additional instruction-following data, question answering, and summarization. ShareGPT training and the original MT-bench, HumanEval, and GSM8K evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains EAGLE, EAGLE-2, and HASS alignment as comparators, and the corresponding retained ablations preserve their comparator membership. The added benchmark and feature-diagnostic tables reuse existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: Table 3 adds speedup measurement and cross-dataset averages to the existing training-step comparison. New evaluations include a four-step InfoNCE diagnostic on 100 randomly selected ShareGPT samples at temperature 0.07 and a Llama3-70B router configuration. The main training and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix D directly tests feature discrepancies across steps for EAGLE-2, HASS, and CSRA. Section 4.2.3 adds a quantitative router-latency analysis, and Appendix F adds a measured Llama3-70B router failure case. These substantially extend analysis of both core components; the earlier router-grid, single-step, and system-prompt studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new diagnostic's 100 sampled examples describe its evaluation sample, not repeated runs or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises EAGLE's temperature-1 results across all six models under unchanged reported settings; for example, Llama2-13B HumanEval changes from 3.47/2.56x to 4.24/3.13x in acceptance length/speedup. v3 also adds Table 3 speedups and averages, Table 6 feature measurements, Table 8 benchmark results, and the 70B router result showing speedup falling from 2.79x to 2.69x.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)-(9) are retained, with no new theorem or proof. The added latency calculations apply existing relations to empirical measurements, and the new feature diagnostic reuses the existing InfoNCE formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same CSRA and LM-head-router contributions, lossless-acceleration claim, and headline 2.50x-4.07x speedup range. The revised conclusion names EAGLE-2 and HASS explicitly without materially changing the claimed contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets two-step CSRA as competitive with four-step HASS, explains the choice of InfoNCE for feature comparison, and quantifies the latency tradeoff behind ineffective routing on a 70B model. These elaborate existing alignment and applicability arguments; the earlier single-step, vocabulary-size, backend, and system-prompt limitations remain.

D1.justification: The new diagnostic documents its random sampling, sample count, step count, and temperature, and Table 9 supplies licenses for the added datasets. Existing loss weights, training data size, hardware, training duration, and repository/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Alpaca, Natural Questions, and CNN/DM and slightly refines the related-work description to include reducing memory access. CORAL's positioning relative to EAGLE, HASS, and other acceleration approaches remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the ablation discussion and appendix additions. The router discussion moves from Appendix D to F, acknowledgments and contact details are added, and the AI-writing-assistance disclosure is removed. Most of the main narrative remains verbatim.

P2.justification: Table 3 becomes a full-width display with speedups and average columns; new Tables 6 and 8 display feature diagnostics and additional benchmarks. Figure 6 is relocated with its plotted content retained, Figure 3 labels are corrected, and the license table expands. The overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: v1 already provides substantial benchmark and ablation evidence. v3 strengthens it with broader task coverage, direct feature-consistency diagnostics, and a measured router failure case that improves practical guidance. These are useful incremental gains, although the new Appendix F incorrectly describes the acceptance-length decrease from 4.23 to 3.93 as 9.3% rather than approximately 7.1%. The added evidence outweighs this localized reporting error.
